title: Casper and the Tryouts
premise: Astrid Reyes, a closeted coder whose anonymous account 'Casper' knows secrets about everyone at Marigold High, finds impossible directions in her late grandmother's recipe box — instructions that fold reality, pulling Astrid and her estranged best friend Theo into a tournament that exists between memory and the present. To get home before graduation, they must win a championship of trials where each round forces them to relive and reveal truths they've buried: the falling-out that ended their friendship, Astrid's secret identity as Casper, and the truth about how their grandmother really died. In the final trial, Astrid must choose between winning the championship that restores her old life or telling the whole school who Casper is; she chooses truth, dissolving the tournament, and graduates having rebuilt her friendship and her self on honest ground.
about_author: Paloma Underhill is a former debate coach from coastal Oregon who writes stories about teenagers who say too much online and not enough out loud. She collects recipe boxes and believes every family keeps one card that isn't about food.

chapters.title: Ninety-Three Days
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She counts down to graduation while posting as Casper, an anonymous account that predicts hallway drama with eerie accuracy. Establishes her isolation, her coding talent, and the cold silence between her and former best friend Theo. Emotional beat: restless dread disguised as control.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Cleaning her grandmother's kitchen, Astrid finds a card titled 'Championship Cake' whose instructions read like coordinates and commands. When she reads them aloud, the kitchen folds sideways. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Folded
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Astrid lands in a bleacher-filled stadium that shouldn't exist, and Theo is pulled in beside her mid-argument. A referee made of static announces the Tryouts have begun. Emotional beat: disorientation and forced proximity.

chapters.title: Rules of Play
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The referee explains: win all five trials before graduation day in the real world, or be 'archived' like other players who came before. Theo recognizes his older brother's name on a memorial wall. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Trial One: The Warm-Up
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The first trial replays the exact moment Astrid and Theo stopped speaking — but this time they must play it to a different ending. They fail twice. Emotional beat: raw embarrassment becoming reluctant teamwork.

chapters.title: Casper Knows
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Between trials, Theo realizes Casper predicted events no algorithm could know — including things only Astrid witnessed. He confronts her; she denies it too quickly. Emotional beat: suspicion rekindling old wounds.

chapters.title: Trial Two: Substitutions
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The trial swaps the players' memories — Astrid lives Theo's worst day, and vice versa. She finally understands why he pulled away after his brother vanished. Emotional beat: empathy arriving through forced embodiment.

chapters.title: The Other Contestants
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They meet rival players: archived kids half-faded into the stands, still trying to win their way back. One, Marisol, warns them the final trial always asks for something you can't take back. Emotional beat: dread and solidarity.

chapters.title: Home Game
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A brief return to the real world reveals only hours passed — but Casper posted during their absence, saying things Astrid never wrote. Something in the tournament is using her account. Emotional beat: violation and paranoia.

chapters.title: Trial Three: The Away Match
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The trial takes place inside Theo's memory of searching for his brother, forcing him to notice details he suppressed — a recipe card clutched in his brother's hand. Emotional beat: guilt transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: Grandma's Card Catalog
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Back home, Astrid decodes more cards and learns her grandmother was a former Tryouts champion who never left cleanly — part of her is still archived. Emotional beat: inherited burden, love complicated by secrets.

chapters.title: Trial Four: Double Headers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Players are paired against versions of themselves. Astrid faces Casper made flesh — every cruel prediction she ever posted, weaponized. Emotional beat: shame confronted head-on.

chapters.title: What Casper Cost
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Astrid confesses everything: Casper is her, the predictions were pattern-hacking plus something stranger — the recipes taught her to read probability. Theo must decide whether the girl who knew everything lied about anything that mattered. Emotional beat: betrayal and its limits.

chapters.title: Rain Delay
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A quiet interlude chapter: the pair shelters in the stadium's concession stand, which recreates her grandmother's kitchen, and cook together from a real recipe for the first time since childhood. Emotional beat: tenderness rebuilding.

chapters.title: Marisol's Forfeit
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Marisol attempts the final trial alone and is archived mid-attempt, leaving behind a note: the championship doesn't matter — winning is the trap. Emotional beat: horror reframing the goal.

chapters.title: The Referee's Face
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid unmasks the static referee: it wears her grandmother's face, grown from the archived fragment. The tournament feeds on unresolved truths, and graduation day is its harvest. Emotional beat: heartbreak and fury.

chapters.title: Championship Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Real-world graduation morning arrives; the final trial begins simultaneously with commencement. The whole school appears in the stands, unaware. Emotional beat: converging pressure, clock ticking.

chapters.title: Trial Five: Sudden Death
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The final trial demands a secret worth archiving them both. Theo offers his brother's fate; the tournament accepts and begins closing over them. Emotional beat: sacrifice without resolution.

chapters.title: Casper Signs Off
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid hijacks the stadium's scoreboard and every screen in school, revealing herself as Casper and confessing every prediction publicly — flooding the tournament with resolved truths it cannot digest. Emotional beat: terror becoming liberation.

chapters.title: Forfeit Victory
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The championship collapses as truths resolve; Astrid refuses the trophy, breaking the harvest cycle. Her grandmother's archived fragment smiles, thanks her, and lets go. Emotional beat: grief braided with release.

chapters.title: Extra Innings
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Back in the real world on graduation afternoon, Theo searches using what he learned and finds his brother alive, archived as a child, returned older and confused but real. Emotional beat: joy earned through loss.

chapters.title: Commencement
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the ceremony, Astrid walks the stage as herself — no handle, no countdown. Theo sits beside her; Marisol's name is read aloud and honored. The recipe box now holds only food. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won belonging.
